A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChatHLS research, with identifiable retained methods and experiments. All text, equations, tables and figures were readable, including v3's Appendices A–H. The supplied v2 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original debugging experiments on 612 cases, HLSFixer ablations, and optimization experiments on five PolyBench kernels.

after.justification: v3 reports original generation, debugging and optimization results, alongside retrieval controls, model-scaling analyses and post-implementation hardware measurements.

M1.justification: v3 extends generation inputs from C algorithms to include natural-language descriptions and changes SFT from LoRA adaptation to full-parameter tuning. The VODA workflow, hierarchical diagnosis/fixing/judging, DPO and three-directive optimization loop remain. The expanded reasoning-to-instruction and QoR-aware reasoning descriptions largely elaborate existing mechanisms.

E1.justification: v3 adds 108 natural-language-to-HLS generation tasks, comprising 85 HLS-Eval designs and 23 custom designs. Optimization expands beyond v2's five linear-algebra kernels to broader kernel workloads and MobileNet and Transformer accelerators. Kernel/Vitis/Manual debugging coverage is retained; changed case counts alone do not establish new coverage.

E2.justification: Debugging comparators change from GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama3.1-8B and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B to Gemini-3-pro, Claude-opus-4.5, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-V3.2. v3 also adds matched RAG variants and C2HLSC/HLSRewriter comparisons; Appendix D.3 identifies the latter baselines as published scores. RALAD and the DSL/learning-based optimization comparators remain.

E3.justification: Training changes from Llama3-8B with 11 SFT/3 DPO epochs to Qwen2.5-Coder-14B with 3/2 epochs; training sample counts and the debugging test size also change. v3 introduces staged pass@k evaluation, matched retrieval controls, an explicit 80% resource ceiling and post-route checks. Optimization is reported as 15 trials, although five-iteration descriptions remain, leaving the exact budget relationship unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained HLSFixer component ablation, v3 adds train–test similarity analysis, controlled retrieval studies, model-family/size sensitivity, token-cost analyses and optimization trajectories in Appendices D–G. Table 4 adds physical-feasibility validation after place-and-route. The per-error analysis expands from 24 displayed error types to 33.

E5.justification: v2 reports aggregate pass rates without repeated-sampling counts or uncertainty bars. v3 specifies five candidates per debugging case and 20 generation repetitions, uses sampled pass@k estimation, and adds error bars to Figure 6 and token-cost Figures 15 and 17. These are newly reported practices; seeds and the statistical meaning of the bars remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Reported debugging performance changes from 82.7% on 612 cases to 93.4% pass@1 on 591 cases. Figure 9's optimization headline changes from 5.4× over baseline on five kernels to 18.1× over broader workloads. These use changed models and evaluation conditions, so they are not same-setting gains. v3 adds generation, accelerator, retrieval and physical-implementation results and removes the energy-efficiency proxy results.

T1.justification: v2's bespoke nonlinear Energy Efficiency definition and its latency/resource penalty construction in Equation 2 are removed. v3 instead formalizes resource-constrained speedup in Appendix D.4. Neither version contains substantive theorems or proofs; the additional standard metric formulas do not constitute a major theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The headline claims expand from debugging and constrained-kernel optimization to demonstrated natural-language generation gains and neural-accelerator optimization. v3 claims a 41.8% relative generation improvement over Gemini-3-pro and replaces v2's 82.7% repair and 3.6× DSL/learning comparison headlines with 32.6% relative debugging improvement and 3.3× over RALAD. The overall ChatHLS purpose remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of retrieval's differing effects on generation and debugging, model-scaling behavior, optimization trajectories and physical feasibility. Appendix G acknowledges greater hardware costs and lower resource efficiency than methods such as Allo. New limitations explicitly identify unsupported DATAFLOW/AXI directives and validation on only one FPGA platform, substantially qualifying v2's generalization discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D newly disclose retrieval chunking, embedding/vector-store choices, top-k retrieval, log parsing, full prompts, teacher inputs, sampling temperatures, detailed SFT/DPO settings, software environment and training durations. These greatly extend v2's brief training description. Appendix H adds asset licensing and intended-use information without establishing a new public artifact release.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 expands positioning beyond retrieval-based assistance to recent LLM-based Bayesian directive optimization and GNN-supervised LIFT, emphasizing design–directive–QoR relationships. References add HLS-Eval, C2HLSC, HLSDebugger and other recent work while removing several earlier general code/HDL and retrieval references. This revises the competitive context beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around three challenges, and contributions are reordered. Method exposition changes from workflow–VODA–HLSFixer–HLSTuner to workflow–HLSTuner–HLSFixer–VODA. Numbered sections, expanded explanations, structured appendices and dedicated limitations/ethics sections substantially reorganize the narrative; author and affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: v3 redraws introductory visuals, expands the optimization chart, and adds generation/accelerator/RAG tables plus prompt, similarity, scaling, cost and trajectory figures. v2's Table 2 is retained as v3's Table 6, and its per-error Figure 6 is expanded and relocated as Figure 14. The energy-efficiency chart is removed, alongside extensive plot and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v2's narrow optimization validation and limited implementation disclosure through broader workloads, matched RAG controls, detailed training/prompt settings and post-place-and-route validation. Explicit applicability limits and resource-cost discussion also improve the paper's qualification of its claims. These provide substantial gains in evidential support and reproducibility, despite unresolved five-versus-fifteen optimization budgets and undefined error bars; higher headline scores alone do not establish the improvement.
